ranking.reason: Losing a lecture recording before notes are made is a sharp, high-stakes fear that a short ad can state in one line, and students hit it every week.
Turning your own PDFs into flashcards and quizzes is an easy-to-grasp promise with frequent need, though free general LLMs such as NotebookLM and ChatGPT reduce the pull to pay for an app.

Lifters who use an Apple Watch feel the lost-set and wrong-exercise bugs mid-workout, but the audience is narrower and the pain reads as a reliability issue rather than something an ad can sell on sight.
Losing or being unable to move flashcard decks hurts, but the complaints come from only three apps and most affected users are loyal to the free incumbent Anki, which lowers the tap rate.

Exact label values with no AI guess is a clear, specific differentiator for people tracking fiber or net carbs, but the audience is niche and large incumbents such as MyFitnessPal and Cronometer make it costly to reach.
Pronunciation judging is a real learner pain, but it is hard to show accuracy in an ad and established brands such as Speak, Babbel and Busuu hold the attention and the trust.
